title: Fix AnthropicClient structured-output schema for dict-valued pose/expression fields
description: Anthropic's output_config.format (native structured outputs) rejects additionalProperties set to a schema (only 'false' is allowed) -- but PosePayload.bone_rotations, PosePayload.ik_targets, and FACSExpression.weights are pydantic Dict[str, ...] fields, which model_json_schema() renders with additionalProperties as an object schema. Confirmed via the opt-in smoke test (RUN_ANTHROPIC_SMOKE_TEST=1) hitting a real 400 BadRequestError: "output_config.format.schema: For 'object' type, 'additionalProperties: object' is not supported". Fix: in AnthropicClient.complete_json (scarecrow_pipeline/nl_appearance.py), build a per-call dynamic schema that replaces each affected dict field's schema with explicit 'properties' entries for exactly the vocabulary's bone/control names (all optional, additionalProperties: false), rather than changing PosePayload/FACSExpression or any downstream consumer.
close_reason: Closed

title: daz_export.py hangs indefinitely on real outfit scenes, ignoring --timeout
description: Live verification (scarecrow-97w) against a real JasonCross+WorkerUniform .duf scene reproduced a hang twice: after launching a genuinely standalone -noPrompt DAZStudio.exe process (confirmed via process creation time + no other running instance to forward IPC to), Daz Studio runs an initial Iray preview/thumbnail render to ~1400-1500 iterations, then goes fully idle (0% CPU, memory flat) and never reaches the point of executing the injected -script (exportToBlender never runs -- no 'Loaded image' or export progress ever appears in Daz's log.txt after the render). subprocess.run(..., timeout=300) in daz_export.py's export_scene() did NOT fire despite the process idling for 11+ minutes past the configured timeout; the wrapper had to be killed manually (Stop-Process -Force) both times. This means the documented CAUTION in daz_export.py ('can crash or silently produce no output') understates the real failure mode -- it can wedge the calling process indefinitely with no automatic recovery. Repro: build a real character+outfit .duf via Daz Studio GUI, close Daz Studio fully (single-instance IPC forwarding otherwise masks this), then run scripts/daz_export.py against it with --timeout 300; observe DAZStudio.exe process persists at 0% CPU well past the timeout.
acceptance_criteria: daz_export.py either (a) reliably raises TimeoutError at ~the configured timeout even when the child process is idle-but-alive rather than exited, e.g. via a hard external watchdog that force-kills the DAZStudio.exe process tree on timeout instead of relying on subprocess.run's own timeout path, or (b) root-causes why the -noPrompt Iray preview render step blocks the script queue for this scene family and fixes that upstream. Verified by re-running the repro above and confirming the wrapper returns (success or a clear TimeoutError) within a bounded time.
notes: Found and fixed a separate, real bug during the same verification session: daz_export.py did not resolve --scene/--out to absolute paths before handing them to Daz Studio, which runs with its own working directory, so a relative path (as shown in docs/outfit-onboarding-workflow.md's own example invocation) could write the .dbz to the wrong place or fail the exists()/non-empty check even on a successful export. Fixed in the same commit as this filing by resolving scene/output_dir to absolute at the top of export_scene(); regression test added in tests/test_daz_export.py.
close_reason: Superseded by decision: no headless DAZ Studio fallback at all. GUI-resident DazScriptServer (scripts/run_diffeomorphic_export.py) is now the sole export path; standalone -noPrompt daz_export.py removed rather than hardened with a watchdog.

title: Implement scripts/generate_sprite_set.py CLI orchestrator
description:
Add scripts/generate_sprite_set.py, a CLI that takes a SpriteSetSpec JSON file (from scarecrow_pipeline/sprite_set.py, T1/scarecrow-scarecrow-uc0.1) and renders every combo.

For each (filename, RenderRequest) from SpriteSetSpec.expand():
1. Write the RenderRequest to a temp/scratch JSON file (e.g. under the spec's output_dir, or Python tempfile -- avoid clobbering between combos)
2. Invoke blender headless once per combo via subprocess: blender --background <scene-or-master-blend> --python blender/worker.py -- --request <request.json>. Follow the exact invocation pattern already used throughout this session (see e.g. how blender/worker.py's own CLI is documented in its module docstring, and how prior validation scripts in this session invoked blender via subprocess with '--' argument separation and ABSOLUTE paths -- a past bug this session found: relative --out-dir/output paths passed to a Blender subprocess can resolve against the wrong drive/cwd in headless mode on Windows; always pass absolute paths).
3. Do NOT try to batch multiple renders inside one Blender process -- worker.py:render() mutates shared scene/compositor/shadow-catcher state in ways not proven safe to call repeatedly in one process. One subprocess per render for this phase.
4. Collect a manifest: list of {combo fields, output_path, status: 'ok'|'failed', stderr on failure} and write it as JSON (e.g. <output_dir>/manifest.json) alongside the rendered PNGs.
5. Surface non-zero subprocess exit codes / stderr clearly per combo rather than failing the whole batch silently or halting on first failure -- continue through the batch and report failures in the manifest.

CLI args: at minimum --spec <spec.json> --blender-exe <path to blender.exe, or read from config/toolchain.json> --master-blend <override, optional>.

- One Blender subprocess per combo, not a shared long-lived process

title: Critique-delta LimbDelta corrections overshoot past centerline now that BICEP_LATERAL anchors sit close to it
description:
Real end-to-end apply_appearance.py --with-critique runs for JasonCross
'standing at ease, arms crossed' (2026-09-17, real Blender 5.1 + real
Anthropic API), done while verifying scarecrow-5mn's anchor-placement fix,
show a NEW, distinct convergence problem: the vision critique's per-limb
LimbDelta corrections (apply_critique_delta in nl_appearance.py) repeatedly
push character_local_offset further across the body than the target
anchor itself, producing a 'shrug'/hands-splayed-outward look on attempt 2
even though attempt 1's anchor placement was directionally correct.

Evidence (multiple runs, same character/description):
- Critique text itself repeatedly CONFIRMS the anchor fix from scarecrow-5mn
  is working: "Hands are correctly anchored to the opposite biceps, but
  large lateral offsets push both hands outward past the body" and
  "forearms overlap but both hands extend straight out past the torso".
- One run's attempt-1 -> attempt-2 delta: left_arm character_local_offset
  went from [0.02, 0.06, -0.05] to [-0.2, 0.16, 0.07] (a -0.375m lateral
  delta), right_arm from [-0.02, 0.0, -0.04] to [0.2, 0.03, 0.04] (a
  +0.425m lateral delta) -- both deltas move the hand further in the SAME
  lateral direction the anchor already crossed to, overshooting well past
  the anchor and toward the opposite shoulder, rather than trimming back
  toward it.

Root cause hypothesis (not yet fixed): for a LimbGoal whose target_anchor
is already on the OPPOSITE side of the body (ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_L/R, as
used for crossed arms), the vision critique model appears to interpret
'bring the hand inward toward the opposite bicep' as 'keep moving further
across', because character_local_offset's sign convention doesn't make
clear that the anchor itself is already past center -- any further
positive delta in that same direction overshoots. This wasn't visible
before scarecrow-5mn's anchor fix because the old anchor sat much further
out (near the elbow), so the same delta magnitude read as 'reaching a bit
further' rather than 'swinging past the body'. See
scarecrow_pipeline/nl_appearance.py's apply_critique_delta and
CritiqueDeltaFeedback/LimbDelta, and anchors.clamp_offset's 0.20m limit
used there (vs. LimbGoal's own 0.15m initial-translation limit).

Fix direction (not yet implemented): either tighten the vision critique's
prompt/schema so it understands the anchor-relative offset sign for an
already-crossed-body anchor, or tighten anchors.clamp_offset's delta-path
limit specifically for ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_L/R, or clamp each LimbDelta's
own magnitude (not just the resulting cumulative offset). Whatever is
tried needs re-verification with a real --with-critique run, same as
scarecrow-5mn.
acceptance_criteria: A real apply_appearance.py --with-critique run for 'arms crossed' passes critique within max_render_attempts=2, using real Blender + real Anthropic API, without the hands overshooting past their target anchors into a shrug/T-pose look.

title: Arm-crossed anchors (ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_L/R) are too far for the opposite arm's 2-bone IK chain to reach naturally
description:
A real end-to-end run of apply_appearance.py --with-critique for JasonCross 'standing at ease, arms crossed' (2026-09-17, real Anthropic API + real Blender 5.1 render, verified after merging the anchor-based rearchitecture from scarecrow-4sm) converged in the RIGHT DIRECTION across both attempts but never passed critique -- the render shows one arm stretched/distorted diagonally across the torso instead of resting naturally crossed.

Root cause, confirmed by dumping IK_Target_*/IK_Pole_* Empty locations from both attempts' saved .blend snapshots:
- Attempt 1: l_forearm target [-0.293, -0.090, 1.217], r_forearm target [0.311, 0.022, 1.235]
- Attempt 2 (after one critique-delta round): l_forearm target [-0.533, -0.200, 1.292], r_forearm target [0.551, 0.072, 1.410]

Both targets moved substantially further across the body between attempts (about +/-0.24m each), in exactly the direction the vision critique prescribed ('right forearm pulls in ~20cm and back ~20cm', etc.) -- so the delta-critique mechanism itself (scarecrow-4sm's actual subject) is working correctly and deterministically, and the fix from that issue's final review (stripping AnthropicClient.critique_pose's JSON schema) is confirmed working end-to-end against the real API.

The remaining problem is anchor placement: ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_L/R (scarecrow_pipeline/anchors.py) resolve to the elbow (l_upperarm/r_upperarm's REST TAIL), which sits laterally far out near the body's outer edge (e.g. r_upperarm rest_tail_world x=-0.3334). For the OPPOSITE forearm's 2-bone IK chain to reach that point, it has to stretch nearly the full width of the torso plus the offset clamp range (+/-0.15 initial, +/-0.20 after a critique delta) on top -- a reach the 2-bone chain (upperarm+forearm) can't make naturally, so Blender's IK solver fully extends/stretches the arm mesh instead of producing a relaxed crossed-arm bend.

Suggested fix direction (not yet implemented): anchor the opposite hand closer to the body centerline instead of the lateral elbow -- e.g. a new anchor interpolated between spine4/chest-center and the SAME-side upperarm's head (shoulder), or partway along the upperarm bone rather than at its tail. Whatever replaces it should be validated with another real --with-critique run before considering this fixed, not just by inspection.
acceptance_criteria: A real apply_appearance.py --with-critique run for 'arms crossed' passes critique (or the vision critique's summary explicitly says the pose now looks correctly crossed/resting, not stretched or distorted) within max_render_attempts=2, using real Blender + real Anthropic API.
notes:
FIXED (verified with real Blender 5.1 + real Anthropic API, 2026-09-17):

1. anchors.py: ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_L/R no longer resolve to the
   upperarm's rest TAIL (the elbow -- the outermost point on that arm,
   too far for the opposite forearm's 2-bone IK chain to reach without
   fully stretching). They now resolve to a new ANCHOR_BLEND_LANDMARKS
   blend: 35% of the way from the upperarm's rest HEAD (shoulder) toward
   its rest TAIL (elbow) -- i.e. much closer to the body centerline, well
   within the opposite chain's max reach (upperarm+forearm bone length).
   resolve_anchor_position/_resolve_bone_point in anchors.py handle both
   simple (bone, point) and blended landmarks; nl_appearance.py's two
   ANCHOR_LANDMARKS[name][0] call sites were updated to a new
   anchors.anchor_required_bones() helper so vocab-availability filtering
   still works for blend anchors.

2. blender/worker.py: removed the "Scarecrow Surface Guard" SHRINKWRAP
   bone constraint added in b6cc75f (explicitly unverified at the time --
   "no Blender in this environment"). Verified now: this guard was the
   ACTUAL primary cause of the severe "one arm stretched/distorted
   diagonally" visual -- disabling it alone (with the OLD far anchor)
   turned a badly broken render into a recognizably crossed-arms pose.
   Removed resolve_body_mesh() too (now dead code, only used by the
   guard).

Verification method: ran scripts/apply_appearance.py --with-critique
for JasonCross 'standing at ease, arms crossed' several times, real
Blender 5.1 + real Anthropic API (see artifacts/scarecrow-5mn_verification/).
Confirmed via direct .blend inspection (IK_Target_*/IK_Pole_* Empty
locations, pose bone head/tail world positions) that:
  - the new anchor's resolved position is within the 2-bone chain's max
    reach (no more full-stretch distortion / disconnected mesh)
  - the vision critique itself repeatedly confirms this: "Hands are
    correctly anchored to the opposite biceps" / "forearms overlap"
  - renders no longer show the original bug's "one arm stretched/
    distorted diagonally across the torso" failure mode

NOT fixed by this issue (filed as scarecrow-p8d instead): the critique-
delta correction step (apply_critique_delta) still sometimes overshoots
the hand past the now-much-closer anchor into a shrug/T-pose look on
attempt 2, so a full --with-critique pass within max_render_attempts=2
isn't yet reliable. That's a distinct bug in the delta-correction
mechanism's offset magnitude/sign handling, not in anchor placement --
see scarecrow-p8d for full evidence and root-cause hypothesis.

test_resolve_anchor_position_blends_bicep_lateral_toward_shoulder, old

(103 passed, 2 skipped) green.

## Phase 1: Semantic Surface Anchors & Coordinate Transform Module

2. Converting between **Character-Local Space** and **Blender World Space**.

```python
# posing/anchors.py
import bpy
from mathutils import Vector, Matrix
from typing import Dict, Tuple

# Pre-defined relative offsets in bone-local space (Rest Pose)
# Format: {Anchor_Name: (parent_bone_name, local_offset_vector)}
DEFAULT_ANCHOR_DEFINITIONS: Dict[str, Tuple[str, Vector]] = {
    # Torso
    "ANCHOR_CHEST_CENTER": ("chest", Vector((0.0, 0.12, 0.05))),
    "ANCHOR_PECTORAL_L": ("chest", Vector((0.08, 0.11, 0.05))),
    "ANCHOR_PECTORAL_R": ("chest", Vector((-0.08, 0.11, 0.05))),
    "ANCHOR_RIBCAGE_MID": ("spine", Vector((0.0, 0.10, 0.0))),
    "ANCHOR_HIP_CREST_L": ("pelvis", Vector((0.16, 0.0, -0.02))),
    "ANCHOR_HIP_CREST_R": ("pelvis", Vector((-0.16, 0.0, -0.02))),
    # Arms / Shoulders
    "ANCHOR_SHOULDER_TOP_L": ("upper_arm.L", Vector((0.0, 0.0, 0.05))),
    "ANCHOR_SHOULDER_TOP_R": ("upper_arm.R", Vector((0.0, 0.0, 0.05))),
    "ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_L": ("upper_arm.L", Vector((0.06, 0.0, -0.12))),
    "ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_R": ("upper_arm.R", Vector((-0.06, 0.0, -0.12))),
    "ANCHOR_FOREARM_VENTRAL_L": ("forearm.L", Vector((0.0, 0.04, -0.10))),
    "ANCHOR_FOREARM_VENTRAL_R": ("forearm.R", Vector((0.0, 0.04, -0.10))),
    # Head / Face
    "ANCHOR_CHIN": ("head", Vector((0.0, 0.09, -0.05))),
    "ANCHOR_TEMPLE_R": ("head", Vector((-0.09, 0.02, 0.04))),
    "ANCHOR_TEMPLE_L": ("head", Vector((0.09, 0.02, 0.04))),
}

def ensure_semantic_anchors(armature_obj: bpy.types.Object) -> Dict[str, bpy.types.Object]:
    """
    Spawns or verifies parented Empty objects for each landmark anchor.
    Anchors move automatically when parent bones animate/deform.
    """
    created_anchors = {}
    
    # Ensure a dedicated collection exists
    anchor_col = bpy.data.collections.get("Rig_Anchors")
    if not anchor_col:
        anchor_col = bpy.data.collections.new("Rig_Anchors")
        bpy.context.scene.collection.children.link(anchor_col)

    for anchor_name, (bone_name, offset) in DEFAULT_ANCHOR_DEFINITIONS.items():
        if bone_name not in armature_obj.pose.bones:
            continue

        empty_name = f"ANCHOR_{armature_obj.name}_{anchor_name}"
        empty_obj = bpy.data.objects.get(empty_name)

        if not empty_obj:
            empty_obj = bpy.data.objects.new(empty_name, None)
            empty_obj.empty_display_type = 'SPHERE'
            empty_obj.empty_display_size = 0.02
            anchor_col.objects.link(empty_obj)

            # Parent to the specific bone
            empty_obj.parent = armature_obj
            empty_obj.parent_type = 'BONE'
            empty_obj.parent_bone = bone_name
            empty_obj.location = offset
        
        created_anchors[anchor_name] = empty_obj

    return created_anchors

def get_character_local_matrix(armature_obj: bpy.types.Object) -> Matrix:
    """
    Returns the transformation matrix defining the Character Coordinate Frame:
      +X : Character's Left
      -X : Character's Right
      +Y : Character's Front (Sagittal Anterior)
      -Y : Character's Back (Sagittal Posterior)
      +Z : Character's Up (Superior)
    """
    root_bone = armature_obj.pose.bones.get("root") or armature_obj.pose.bones.get("pelvis")
    if root_bone:
        return armature_obj.matrix_world @ root_bone.matrix
    return armature_obj.matrix_world

def local_offset_to_world(armature_obj: bpy.types.Object, offset_vec: Vector) -> Vector:
    """Transforms a delta offset from Character-Local space to Blender World space."""
    char_matrix = get_character_local_matrix(armature_obj)
    rotation_scale = char_matrix.to_3x3()
    return rotation_scale @ offset_vec
```

## Phase 2: LLM JSON Schema & Translation Layer

Create `posing/schemas.py`. Disallow arbitrary world $[x, y, z]$ floats in the output. The LLM must choose a discrete semantic anchor, a layer depth (outer vs. inner for arm clearance), and a character-local micro-offset.

```python
# posing/schemas.py
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List, Literal, Optional

AnchorEnum = Literal[
    "ANCHOR_CHEST_CENTER",
    "ANCHOR_PECTORAL_L",
    "ANCHOR_PECTORAL_R",
    "ANCHOR_RIBCAGE_MID",

    "ANCHOR_HIP_CREST_R",
    "ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_L",
    "ANCHOR_BICEP_LATERAL_R",
    "ANCHOR_FOREARM_VENTRAL_L",
    "ANCHOR_FOREARM_VENTRAL_R",
    "ANCHOR_CHIN",
    "ANCHOR_TEMPLE_R",
    "ANCHOR_TEMPLE_L"
]

ElbowPoleStrategy = Literal[

    "OUTWARD",       # T-pose, fighting stance
    "DOWN_PINNED",   # Hands at sides

]

HandShapeEnum = Literal[
    "RELAXED_CUP",
    "FIST_SOFT",
    "OPEN_FLAT_TOUCH",
    "POINTING_INDEX",
    "GRASP_BICEP"
]

class LimbGoal(BaseModel):
    target_anchor: AnchorEnum = Field(..., description="Target anatomical surface anchor.")
    character_local_offset: List[float] = Field(
        default=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
        description="Offset [dx, dy, dz] in meters in character space (+X=Left, +Y=Front, +Z=Up). Keep values between -0.15 and 0.15."
    )
    layer_depth: Literal["inner", "outer", "neutral"] = Field(
        default="neutral",
        description="For crossed arms/legs. 'outer' limb is pushed +4cm forward automatically to clear the other limb."
    )
    elbow_strategy: ElbowPoleStrategy = Field(default="DOWN_FORWARD")
    hand_shape: HandShapeEnum = Field(default="RELAXED_CUP")

class FullBodyPoseIntent(BaseModel):
    pose_name: str
    weight_stance: Literal["neutral", "shift_left", "shift_right"] = Field(default="neutral")
    spine_twist_degrees: float = Field(default=0.0, description="Rotation of upper torso relative to hips.")
    left_arm: Optional[LimbGoal] = None
```

## Phase 3: IK Runtime, Surface Snapping & Clavicle Logic

Create `posing/ik_runtime.py`. This executes the resolved targets in Blender and uses Blender constraints to prevent torso penetration and auto-protract clavicles.

```python
# posing/ik_runtime.py
import bpy
from mathutils import Vector, Euler
from math import radians
from .schemas import FullBodyPoseIntent, LimbGoal
from .anchors import ensure_semantic_anchors, local_offset_to_world

def apply_pose_to_g9(
    armature_obj: bpy.types.Object,
    body_mesh_obj: bpy.types.Object,
    pose_intent: FullBodyPoseIntent
):
    anchors = ensure_semantic_anchors(armature_obj)
    
    # 1. Weight shift and spine line of action
    _apply_torso_dynamics(armature_obj, pose_intent)

    # 2. Clavicle Protraction (Crucial for crossing arms without socket distortion)
    if pose_intent.left_arm and pose_intent.right_arm:
        if pose_intent.left_arm.layer_depth in ["inner", "outer"] and \
           pose_intent.right_arm.layer_depth in ["inner", "outer"]:
            _protract_clavicles(armature_obj, forward_deg=12.0, elevation_deg=6.0)

    # 3. Apply Left Arm
    if pose_intent.left_arm:
        _apply_limb_ik(
            armature_obj=armature_obj,
            body_mesh_obj=body_mesh_obj,
            limb="L",
            goal=pose_intent.left_arm,
            anchors=anchors
        )

    # 4. Apply Right Arm
    if pose_intent.right_arm:
        _apply_limb_ik(
            armature_obj=armature_obj,
            body_mesh_obj=body_mesh_obj,
            limb="R",
            goal=pose_intent.right_arm,
            anchors=anchors
        )
        
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()

def _apply_limb_ik(
    armature_obj: bpy.types.Object,
    body_mesh_obj: bpy.types.Object,
    limb: str,
    goal: LimbGoal,
    anchors: dict
):
    # Locate Diffeomorphic IK target and Pole bone controls
    # Default Diffeomorphic / MHX rig bone naming:
    ik_target_bone = armature_obj.pose.bones.get(f"hand.ik.{limb}") or armature_obj.pose.bones.get(f"IK_hand.{limb}")
    pole_bone = armature_obj.pose.bones.get(f"elbow_pole.{limb}") or armature_obj.pose.bones.get(f"pole_elbow.{limb}")

    if not ik_target_bone or goal.target_anchor not in anchors:
        return

    anchor_obj = anchors[goal.target_anchor]
    
    # Base target position from semantic anchor
    target_pos = anchor_obj.matrix_world.translation.copy()

    # Apply character-local offsets
    local_offset = Vector(goal.character_local_offset)
    
    # Auto-separate forearm collision via layer depth
    if goal.layer_depth == "outer":
        local_offset.y += 0.05  # Push forward 5cm along character anterior axis
    elif goal.layer_depth == "inner":
        local_offset.y -= 0.02  # Tuck closer to chest

    world_offset = local_offset_to_world(armature_obj, local_offset)
    final_ik_pos = target_pos + world_offset

    # Position the IK control
    ik_target_bone.matrix.translation = final_ik_pos

    # Attach/Update Shrinkwrap Constraint on IK bone to prevent mesh penetration
    _ensure_surface_limit(armature_obj, ik_target_bone, body_mesh_obj)

    # Resolve Elbow Pole Vector
    if pole_bone:
        _position_pole(armature_obj, pole_bone, ik_target_bone, limb, goal.elbow_strategy)

def _ensure_surface_limit(armature_obj: bpy.types.Object, pose_bone: bpy.types.PoseBone, body_mesh: bpy.types.Object):
    """Adds a non-penetration Limit Distance constraint against the deformed body surface."""
    constraint_name = "Surface_Collision_Guard"
    con = pose_bone.constraints.get(constraint_name)
    if not con:
        con = pose_bone.constraints.new(type='SHRINKWRAP')
        con.name = constraint_name
        con.target = body_mesh
        con.shrinkwrap_type = 'NEAREST_SURFACE'
        con.distance = 0.03  # Maintain 3cm distance outside the skin
        con.influence = 0.8  # Soft blend to avoid sudden popping

def _position_pole(armature_obj, pole_bone, ik_bone, limb: str, strategy: str):
    shoulder = armature_obj.pose.bones.get(f"upper_arm.{limb}")
    if not shoulder:
        return
    
    s_pos = shoulder.matrix.translation
    h_pos = ik_bone.matrix.translation
    mid = (s_pos + h_pos) * 0.5

    char_matrix = armature_obj.matrix_world
    forward = (char_matrix.to_3x3() @ Vector((0, 1, 0))).normalized()
    down = (char_matrix.to_3x3() @ Vector((0, 0, -1))).normalized()
    outward = (char_matrix.to_3x3() @ Vector((1 if limb == 'L' else -1, 0, 0))).normalized()

    if strategy == "DOWN_FORWARD":
        pole_bone.matrix.translation = mid + (down * 0.25) + (forward * 0.15)
    elif strategy == "OUTWARD":
        pole_bone.matrix.translation = mid + (outward * 0.35)
    elif strategy == "DOWN_PINNED":
        pole_bone.matrix.translation = mid + (down * 0.35)
    else:
        pole_bone.matrix.translation = mid + (down * 0.20)

def _protract_clavicles(armature_obj: bpy.types.Object, forward_deg: float, elevation_deg: float):
    for limb, sign in [("L", 1), ("R", -1)]:
        clavicle = armature_obj.pose.bones.get(f"clavicle.{limb}")
        if clavicle:
            clavicle.rotation_mode = 'XYZ'
            clavicle.rotation_euler = Euler((
                radians(elevation_deg),
                0.0,
                radians(forward_deg * sign)
            ), 'XYZ')

def _apply_torso_dynamics(armature_obj: bpy.types.Object, intent: FullBodyPoseIntent):
    pelvis = armature_obj.pose.bones.get("pelvis")
    if pelvis and intent.weight_stance != "neutral":
        shift_amount = 0.04 if intent.weight_stance == "shift_left" else -0.04
        pelvis.location.x += shift_amount
        # Counter-tilt spine
        spine = armature_obj.pose.bones.get("spine")
        if spine:
            spine.rotation_mode = 'XYZ'
            spine.rotation_euler.z = radians(-3.0 if intent.weight_stance == "shift_left" else 3.0)
```

## Phase 4: Local Delta-Critique Loop

Create `posing/critique_optimizer.py`. This state machine retains the current pose state and sends explicit local coordinate delta instructions to the Vision LLM.

```python
# posing/critique_optimizer.py
import json
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List, Optional
from .schemas import FullBodyPoseIntent

class LimbDelta(BaseModel):
    limb: str = Field(..., description="'left_arm' or 'right_arm'")
    delta_meters: List[float] = Field(
        ...,
        description="Relative adjustment in meters [dx, dy, dz] in Character Space: +X=Left, +Y=Front, +Z=Up."
    )
    change_anchor: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Optional new Anchor Enum if target is completely off.")
    notes: str

class CritiqueDeltaFeedback(BaseModel):
    pose_is_satisfactory: bool
    critique_summary: str
    adjustments: List[LimbDelta]

def apply_critique_delta(current_pose: FullBodyPoseIntent, feedback: CritiqueDeltaFeedback) -> FullBodyPoseIntent:
    """
    Applies corrective vector deltas iteratively without re-deriving coordinates from scratch.
    """
    new_pose = current_pose.copy(deep=True)

    for adj in feedback.adjustments:
        limb_goal = getattr(new_pose, adj.limb, None)
        if not limb_goal:
            continue

        if adj.change_anchor:
            limb_goal.target_anchor = adj.change_anchor

        # Apply simple vector addition in local character space
        limb_goal.character_local_offset[0] += adj.delta_meters[0]
        limb_goal.character_local_offset[1] += adj.delta_meters[1]
        limb_goal.character_local_offset[2] += adj.delta_meters[2]

        # Clamp offsets to safe ranges (-20cm to +20cm from landmark)
        for i in range(3):
            limb_goal.character_local_offset[i] = max(-0.20, min(0.20, limb_goal.character_local_offset[i]))

    return new_pose
```

description: Running scripts/apply_appearance.py --character JasonCross --description 'standing at ease, arms crossed, jaw slightly open' against the real Anthropic API produces a rendered pose where the arms are held out/bent oddly near the hips/chest -- not visually 'arms crossed' -- even after fixing a real rotation-order bug in the system prompt (see commit fixing nl_appearance.py's build_system_prompt: it previously told the model to reorder the [x,y,z] triplet per each bone's rotation_mode letter order, but blender/worker.py:138 assigns bone.rotation_euler = Vector(euler) literally -- value[0] is always X, [1] always Y, [2] always Z regardless of rotation_mode, which only affects Blender's internal composition order). That fix is correct and worth keeping, but a second real-API test after applying it still produced a non-crossed-arms pose with different (still wrong) numeric values. Root cause: the model has no calibrated ground truth for what rotation values actually achieve a given pose on this specific rig -- docs/posable_bones.json's rotation_limits_radians is null for every bone, and build_system_prompt has no worked numeric example. Two possible directions for a real fix, not yet attempted: (1) check whether the daz-pose-indexer skill's indexed pose library has a real 'arms crossed' reference pose whose bone values could calibrate the prompt or serve as a verification reference; (2) iterate via multiple real-API-call + Blender-render round trips, tuning prompt guidance by trial and error (costs real API/render time per round, not guaranteed to converge). Needs a dedicated session with render-viewing in the loop, not a quick fix.
close_reason: Root cause fixed: switched limb posing from blind FK Euler guessing to IK targets + pole targets + rest-pose spatial landmarks (docs/posable_bones.json's rest_head_world/rest_tail_world), with a render->vision-critique->retry loop (scarecrow_pipeline/pose_critique.py) so mismatches are caught instead of silently accepted. Verified against the real Anthropic API and real Blender renders: the original bug class (elbows bent wildly/unstably near the hips or chest) is gone -- elbow bend direction is now stable via pole targets, and IK targets land in the correct general chest-height region using the new landmarks. Full 'arms crossed' visual precision for a tight bimanual gesture still needs more than prompt tuning (the LLM can't reliably reason to exact tucked/stacked hand coordinates from verbal guidance alone, even with a worked example) -- tracked as a distinct follow-up, scarecrow-4sm, proposing numeric (not just prose) feedback on retry.

title: Implement scripts/onboard_character.py orchestrator
description: Add scripts/onboard_character.py per scarecrow-09e: pure orchestration CLI that chains the existing standalone steps for onboarding a new character into the master-cache registry -- no new render logic. title: Add --collection-name normalization to blender/import_daz_artifact.py
description: import_daz_artifact.py currently imports a character DBZ and saves the .blend without giving the resulting top-level collection a known name. scarecrow_pipeline/registry.py's CharacterRecord.collection field needs to record that name, and worker.py's append_collection()/resolve_armature() require the character to be a single named top-level collection in master_blend. blender/import_environment_asset.py already establishes the normalize-after-import pattern (collection_utils.py snapshot/diff helpers) for Environment_<name>; do the analogous thing here but by wrapping the new top-level collection(s) DAZ's importer created (not flattening objects, since author_outfit_variant.py later nests Outfit_/Hair_ variant collections under this one and relies on the nested structure from bpy.data.libraries.load surviving). Add an optional --collection-name arg; when given, snapshot bpy.context.scene.collection.children before import, wrap whatever new top-level collections appear after import into one collection named --collection-name, and print CHARACTER_COLLECTION <name> so callers can parse it. description: Headless verification of render_scene() (scarecrow-e1x/render_scene issue) using two character placements -- either a real second character from Phase 2/4 onboarding or two placements of Jason Cross as a stand-in. title: Make scarecrow_pipeline/__init__.py lazy to avoid forcing pydantic inside Blender's bundled Python
description: blender/import_environment_asset.py had to bypass scarecrow_pipeline's package __init__ via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location to reach the bpy-free environment_asset.py module, because scarecrow_pipeline/__init__.py eagerly imports schemas.py (pydantic-dependent), and Blender's bundled Python has no pydantic installed. File before Phase 3 needs Registry from inside Blender.

title: Document/streamline DAZ-side outfit onboarding workflow (scene-first, headless export)
description: Onboarding a new outfit/hair variant currently requires manually driving a live DAZ Studio GUI session (loading pieces via Smart Content, confirming auto-fit dialogs, saving the scene) before author_outfit_variant.py can run. This is fragile: DAZ Studio is single-threaded, and an unexpected auto-fit confirmation dialog can hang or crash the app with no recovery (observed during scarecrow-2oz's Worker Uniform onboarding). We settled on a simpler model: the workflow should start from a .duf scene the user has already built (character + outfit already applied), not from scripted content-library loading. Formalize that as the supported workflow -- document it, and/or write a small headless .dsa script (invoked like scripts/daz_export.py already launches DAZ Studio non-interactively) that takes an already-prepared scene .duf and exports the .dbz, replacing any need to drive the live GUI or content manager programmatically.
design:
Keep DAZ Studio's role limited to: user builds/saves the scene manually, then a non-interactive DAZ Studio invocation (-noPrompt -script, matching scripts/daz_export.py's pattern) runs the export_to_blender.dsa export logic against that saved .duf and exits. No content-mgr openFile() calls, no auto-fit dialog handling needed.

CAUTION: DAZ Studio's -noPrompt headless/batch mode is itself fragile -- it can crash or silently fail to produce output on some scenes/machines, independent of the auto-fit dialog issue this workflow avoids. Don't assume 'headless' == 'reliable'; the scripted export step still needs a real failure check (verify the expected .dbz was written, non-zero size, timeout handling like scripts/daz_export.py's subprocess.run(timeout=...)) and a documented fallback of running the same export interactively if headless mode misbehaves.
acceptance_criteria: A documented (or scripted) path exists for outfit onboarding that starts from a user-prepared .duf scene and produces the .dbz without requiring live DazScriptServer manipulation of DAZ Studio's content manager or scene graph.
close_reason: Formalized the scene-first onboarding workflow in docs/outfit-onboarding-workflow.md, linked from README. Rewrote scripts/daz_export.py to strip Diffeomorphic export_to_blender.dsa's interactive createDialog() entry point (shared build_headless_script() extracted to new scripts/daz_headless_script.py, reused by run_diffeomorphic_export.py) so it runs headlessly against an already-saved .duf via -noPrompt with no content-manager/scene-graph scripting needed. Added the CAUTION-mandated real failure check: verifies the expected .dbz was actually written and non-empty (previously the trailing output_dir CLI arg was silently unused by the dsa, so the wrapper couldn't actually tell success from silent failure). Added tests/test_daz_export.py (3 tests, mocked subprocess) covering success, silent-failure, and nonzero-exit paths; full suite (13 tests) passes. NOTE: could not verify against a live Daz Studio instance in this session (daz-api/vangard-daz-mcp MCP servers were disconnected) -- the -noPrompt CLI invocation and headless-script patching logic are unit-tested and reuse the same string-patching approach already used successfully via the live DazScriptServer path, but an end-to-end run against real Daz Studio is still needed to fully close the loop; flagging for human verification on next Worker Uniform-style outfit onboarding.

Bug to fix first: apply_pose/apply_expression in worker.py grab the FIRST armature in the scene (next(obj for obj in bpy.data.objects if obj.type=='ARMATURE')) -- correct for one character, silently wrong for N; must become explicitly per-character. Add scarecrow_pipeline/schemas.py:SceneRequest (new, additive -- RenderRequest untouched): characters: list[CharacterPlacement] (character/master_blend/outfit/hair/pose/expression + world-space placement transform) + shared camera/lighting + background: BackgroundSpec (union of image_plate mode reusing compositor.py AlphaOver extended for N characters, and 3d_environment mode with no 2D compositing, characters positioned into a pre-imported environment collection from Phase 4). title: resolve_pose_intent/anchors.py raise bare KeyError instead of AppearanceTranslationError for incomplete vocabularies
description: scarecrow_pipeline/nl_appearance.py's _available_anchor_names (and anchors.resolve_anchor_position) only check that an anchor's landmark BONE NAME is present in a given AppearanceVocabulary, not that the bone's entry actually carries rest_head_world/rest_tail_world -- a vocab with an incomplete bone entry raises a bare KeyError deep inside anchor resolution instead of the module's normal AppearanceTranslationError. A WIDER, related hole: resolve_pose_intent unconditionally dereferences bone_landmarks[anchors.LIMB_BONES[side]['shoulder_bone']]['rest_head_world'] for the shoulder-pole landmark, with no availability check at all (unlike the anchor's own landmark bone, which build_user_prompt/_available_anchor_names DO filter) -- so a vocab missing l_upperarm/r_upperarm crashes the same way even if the anchor itself was 'available'. Also: a vocab with none of the landmark bones present produces an empty enum ([]) in the schema sent to the LLM for target_anchor, which is invalid JSON Schema (enum requires >=1 item). Real-world risk is low (the actual docs/posable_bones.json always has complete entries for every bone), but this is a legitimate robustness gap flagged by two separate task reviews during scarecrow-4sm's implementation and by its final whole-branch review, deferred as non-blocking each time. Fix: one precondition check in resolve_pose_intent (or a shared helper) that validates a vocab has everything a requested LimbGoal/weight_stance/clavicle-protraction resolution needs before touching it, raising a clean, catchable error instead of a bare KeyError; also guard the empty-enum case.
acceptance_criteria: A vocab missing l_upperarm/r_upperarm/rest_head_world/rest_tail_world triggers a caught, descriptive error (not a bare KeyError) somewhere in translate_appearance's flow, with a regression test.

title: CritiqueDeltaFeedback.change_anchor lacks enum constraint; a malformed critique verdict crashes run_with_critique instead of degrading
description: scarecrow_pipeline/nl_appearance.py: LimbGoal.target_anchor is constrained to anchors.ANCHOR_NAMES in the JSON schema sent to the LLM (via _localize_open_maps), but LimbDelta.change_anchor is not -- it's only validated client-side by a field_validator after the fact. If AnthropicClient.critique_pose's structured-extraction call emits an invalid change_anchor, CritiqueDeltaFeedback.model_validate(verdict_raw) raises an uncaught ValidationError that propagates out of run_with_critique/apply_appearance, aborting the whole run even though an expensive render already succeeded -- contradicting the module's own documented promise ('Never raises on a critique mismatch... so a human or CI can still inspect the artifact'). Flagged by the final whole-branch review during scarecrow-4sm's implementation; deferred as non-blocking since it requires a specific malformed model response to trigger. Fix: inject the anchor enum into change_anchor's schema the same way target_anchor gets it, and/or catch a malformed verdict in run_with_critique and treat it as pose_is_satisfactory=True with the parse error folded into critique_summary.

title: AnthropicClient: array-of-pairs wire shape scales, but grammar-size limits still unverified at edges
description: translate_appearance's LLM wire schema now uses an array-of-{name,value} shape (with a single name enum) for bone_rotations/ik_targets/weights instead of one property per vocabulary entry, fixing a 'compiled grammar is too large' 400 from the real Anthropic API at production vocab size (143 bones, 446 FACS controls) -- verified end-to-end against the real API. Not yet verified: whether Anthropic's enum-size limit itself has a ceiling that could still be hit with a larger future vocabulary (e.g. if facs_controls.json grows well past 446), and whether MAX_ATTEMPTS retries with a full-size schema meaningfully increase latency/cost per apply_appearance.py call. Not urgent; file for future awareness only.

title: Reconsider AnthropicClient default model, max_tokens, and structured output approach
description: AnthropicClient defaults to model claude-sonnet-5 and max_tokens 4096, using forced tool use for structured JSON output.
